::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Started 2026-10-14.** The taxonomy in Section 3 is a first list, written
from the tools on the [Pharmacometrics Tools](../../pmx-tools.qmd) page and
not yet checked against published frameworks. The project's earlier
question, validating code an agent wrote, is now
[one document](agent-written-code.qmd) under this one.
:::

## 1. Goal

Two deliverables:

1. A taxonomy of what gets validated in a pharmacometrics (PMX) activity,
   with the tools that already exist for each kind and the gaps where none
   does.
2. A validation plan template: for any activity, which kinds of validation
   apply, which tool checks each, how deep the check goes given the risk,
   and who does it.

Both are meant for work done by anyone: a coding agent, an intern, a
postdoc, a junior or a senior associate.

Out of scope:

- **Evaluating an AI model in general**, such as benchmarks. The question is
  whether one analysis is right.
- **Computerized system validation** in the regulatory sense, such as 21 CFR
  Part 11 for software that handles clinical records.
- **Writing the missing tools.** This project finds the gaps and ranks them.
  Filling one becomes its own project.

## 2. One Plan for Any Author

The validation an analysis needs is set by the analysis and by the cost of
getting it wrong, and the same questions apply whoever did the work. What
changes with the author is where errors are expected, and so which checks
carry the most weight. The rows below are a working guess.

| Author | Errors to expect | Where the weight goes |
|---|---|---|
| Coding agent | Code that runs cleanly and computes the wrong quantity; a silent change to data handling; a fluent summary of a paper it misread | Independent reproduction of the main results; checks on outputs; claims against sources |
| Intern or new hire | Not knowing what a plausible parameter value looks like; unfamiliar data conventions; not asking | The model's plausibility; the data; whether the result answers the question |
| Experienced modeler | Template code reused where it does not fit; assumed data conventions; the question drifting during the work | The question; the data |

: Where errors are expected, by author {tbl-colwidths="[20,45,35]"}

Working with a person and working with an agent share the same steps. Each
needs background, instructions, checking and correction, and the steps
differ in where the result is kept.

| Step | A person | An agent |
|---|---|---|
| Background | Onboarding, a reading list, the team's conventions | Skill files and instruction files such as `CLAUDE.md` |
| Instructions | The specification | The same specification |
| Checking | The validation plan | The same validation plan |
| Correction | Feedback, which the person carries forward | A change to the skill or instruction file; anything not written down is gone next session |
| Explaining the work later | Can be asked, and the final presentation of an internship tests it | Only what is in the record |

: The steps of working with a person and with an agent {tbl-colwidths="[20,40,40]"}

The checking row is what this project is about. An intern who directs an
agent is also the agent's first reviewer, which makes the validation plan
part of what an intern learns. The
[PMX internship specification](../pmx-internship/specification.qmd) uses
this.

## 3. The Taxonomy

Eleven kinds of validation, in the order an analysis meets them. The table is
the summary; each kind has a subsection below with the same three parts.

| # | Kind | Asks | Existing tools | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Question | Is this the right question for the decision? | Context of Use table, Dose Finding Framework | No check after the work |
| 2 | Causal assumptions | What causes what, and could a confounder explain the relationship the model estimates? | Causality checklist, causal diagrams talk | Not yet a step in any plan |
| 3 | Sources | Does each claim say what the source says? | Status markers in `references.qmd`, Reading Papers guide | Not a portable tool |
| 4 | Data | Is the analysis dataset the right one, built correctly? | Validation checklist (import, modify), xGx | No dataset assembly checklist |
| 5 | Code | Does the code compute what it claims? | R coding checklist, Validation checklist | Agent-written code |
| 6 | Model | Does the model describe the data, with plausible parameters? | ggPMX, xgxr, See-Value | No model evaluation checklist |
| 7 | Predictions | Is the uncertainty in a prediction stated, and does the model predict better than a simple benchmark? | Uncertainty cheat sheet and checklist, pedigree table, Stein and Looby 2018 | No benchmarking procedure |
| 8 | Conclusions | Does the conclusion follow from the result? | Causality checklist, and the diagram from kind 2 | To assess |
| 9 | Communication | Do the figures and slides show what was found, without overstating it? | Graphics principles cheat sheet, Presentation checklist, evaluation form | Written reports |
| 10 | Reproducibility | Can someone else rerun it and get the same numbers, and is there a record of what was checked? | Validation checklist | Record of an agent session |
| 11 | Use | Was the answer used for the decision it was meant for? | None | No follow-up practice |

: Eleven kinds of validation and the tools for each {tbl-colwidths="[4,14,30,32,20]"}

Kinds 5, 6 and 7 are the three the project started from: the R coding
checklist, the diagnostic plots, and the uncertainty checklist. The other
eight are added here, and Section 6 question 4 asks whether eleven is
complete.

### 3.1 Question

**Asks.** Is this the right question for the decision, with a named person
who will use the answer, and is the analysis sized to it?

**Existing tools.**

- [Context of Use table](../../references/ContextOfUse_Table_1page.pdf),
  for scoping a modeling activity.
- [Dose Finding Framework](https://ascpt.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/psp4.12701).
- The [Annual Planning](../strat-planning/index.qmd) project, at the level
  of a year's decisions.

**Gap.** All three are used before the work. Nothing checks at the end that
the answer still answers the question asked at the start.

### 3.2 Causal Assumptions

**Asks.** What causes what in the system the analysis describes, and could
a variable that affects both the exposure and the response explain the
relationship the model estimates? Such a variable is a confounder. In an
exposure-response analysis of a monoclonal antibody, sicker patients often
clear the drug faster, so they have lower exposure and worse outcomes, and
the analysis sees exposure predicting response where disease severity is
driving both.

The check is to draw a causal diagram for the question before the data are
analyzed, with an arrow from each cause to each effect, and to look in it for
paths from exposure to response that do not go through the drug's effect.
Each such path is a confounder to adjust for, or a reason the analysis
cannot answer the causal question as asked.

**Existing tools.**

- Causality Checklist and Guidance for PMX:
  [PDF](../../files/causality-checklist.pdf) ·
  [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Hc3RoTJXS-PQCUm-rG_RCuEa3ykRj5FiAtqRwgSiX6M/edit).
- [Causal diagrams for understanding when correlation doesn't imply causation](../../files/2021-10-12-causal-diagrams.pdf),
  a 2021 talk.

**Gap.** The tools exist and are not a step in any plan. The proposal here
is that every validation plan carries this row, and that the row holds
either a causal diagram or a sentence saying why the question needs none,
such as a randomized dose comparison where dose is the only exposure. Kind 7
asks how uncertain an analysis's assumptions are; this kind asks whether the
causal structure behind them is right. Whether every model needs a diagram is
Section 6 question 6.

### 3.3 Sources

**Asks.** Does each claim drawn from a paper, a label or a regulatory review
say what the source says?

**Existing tools.**

- The status markers this site's projects put on every entry of a
  `references.qmd` (❌ not checked, ⚠️ transcribed and unverified, ✅
  checked), shaped as in
  [the TCE-IPDE references](../tce-ipde/references.qmd).
- The [Reading Papers](../../guides/reading-papers.qmd) guide.

**Gap.** The markers are a convention of this repository, not a tool someone
else can pick up. There is no procedure for checking an agent's summary of a
paper, which is where this check is most often skipped.

### 3.4 Data

**Asks.** Is the analysis dataset built from the right files and versions,
are doses, times, missing values and values below the limit of
quantification handled as intended, and do derived variables and exclusions
match the plan?

**Existing tools.**

- The [Validation Checklist](../../references/Validation_Checklist.pdf),
  sections on importing and modifying data.
- [xGx](http://opensource.nibr.com/xgx) exploratory graphics, which show the
  data before any model sees it.

**Gap.** No checklist for assembling a PMX analysis dataset against its data
specification: dosing records, event types, time since first dose, covariate
merges. Errors here run cleanly through every later step.

### 3.5 Code

**Asks.** Does the code compute what it claims to, can someone else read it,
and does it run cleanly from the start?

**Existing tools.**

- R Coding Checklist:
  [PDF](../../files/r-coding-checklist.pdf) ·
  [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/17ec8YaARWZ6wppv3AfZCdaHfPwvOFUABXyXmENgHnpE/edit).
- The [Validation Checklist](../../references/Validation_Checklist.pdf),
  whose planning section chooses the depth of review from the risk: unit
  tests, spot checks, code review, rerunning step by step, or independent
  reproduction.

**Gap.** Both assume a person wrote the code and a second person reviews it.
[Validating Code Written by an AI Agent](agent-written-code.qmd) works out
what changes when an agent is the author.

### 3.6 Model

**Asks.** Does the model describe the data, and are its parameters plausible?
The usual diagnostics: goodness-of-fit plots, residuals (conditional
weighted residuals, normalized prediction distribution errors), visual
predictive checks, parameter precision, shrinkage, and parameter values
against physiology and published models.

**Existing tools.**

- [ggPMX](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ggPMX) for diagnostic plots, and
  [xgxr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=xgxr).
- [See-Value](https://www.see-value.com), for lineups: the real data's plot
  hidden among plots simulated from the model, to see whether a viewer can
  pick it out.
- The model evaluation skill planned in
  [Pharmacometrics modeling skills](../ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/index.qmd).

**Gap.** No written model evaluation checklist. The skills project is
writing one for an agent, and the same text could serve a person. Plausibility
against prior knowledge is the part least covered by any plot.

### 3.7 Predictions

**Asks.** Two questions. Is the uncertainty in a prediction stated,
including the uncertainty from assumptions and not only from parameter
estimates, and is the prediction inside the range the data support? And
does the model predict better than a simple one would? A complex model, such
as a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model, is checked by fitting a
simple model to the same data and comparing how well each predicts data
neither was fitted to: a later cohort, a new dose, another study. If the
simple model predicts as well, the complex model's extra structure is not
what the prediction rests on.

**Existing tools.**

- [Uncertainty Cheat Sheet and Checklist](https://zenodo.org/records/4409236).
- [Uncertainty Assessment Pedigree Table](../../references/Uncertainty_Assessment_Pedigree_Table.pdf),
  which grades each input by the strength of the evidence behind it.
- [Presentation on Managing Uncertainty](../../references/Uncertainty_Assessment_Presentation.pdf).
- Stein and Looby (2018),
  [Benchmarking QSP models against simple models: a path to improved comprehension and predictive performance](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Benchmarking+QSP+models+against+simple+models),
  *CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology* 7:487–489. The citation is
  taken from a later paper's reference list and has not been checked against
  the journal.

**Gap.** The paper is an argument for benchmarking, not a procedure: which
simple model to pick, which data to hold out, and what difference in
predictive performance counts. Writing that down is the gap. The
uncertainty checklist also needs checking for extrapolation, to doses,
populations or durations outside the data.

### 3.8 Conclusions

**Asks.** Does the conclusion follow from the result? A model can be right
and the claim drawn from it wrong, most often a causal claim from
observational exposure-response data. Kind 2 sets up the causal diagram at
the start; this kind checks the final claims against it.

**Existing tools.**

- The causal diagram from kind 2, which a causal claim is checked against,
  and the Causality Checklist that goes with it (3.2).

**Gap.** To assess. Multiple comparisons and selective reporting are not
obviously covered by anything listed here.

### 3.9 Communication

**Asks.** Do the figures, slides and report show what the analysis found,
with the uncertainty, and without overstating it?

**Existing tools.**

- [Graphics Principles Cheat Sheet](../../references/Graphics_Principles_Cheat_Sheet_v1.1.pdf).
- [Presentation Checklist](../../references/Presentation_Checklist_v2.03.pdf)
  and the Presentation Evaluation Feedback Form:
  [PDF](../../files/presentation-evaluation-form.pdf) ·
  [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1K_lcsG6sClLQcd5sm_ezcvtD9ccmm0uM/edit).

**Gap.** Nothing for a written report. This repository's writing guide does
part of the job for an agent's drafts, and is not written for a reviewer.

### 3.10 Reproducibility

**Asks.** Can someone else rerun the analysis from its inputs and get the
same numbers, and is there a record of what was checked, by whom?

**Existing tools.**

- The [Validation Checklist](../../references/Validation_Checklist.pdf),
  overall section.
- Version control, and on this site the frozen computation cache, which
  replays a page's results exactly.

**Gap.** When an agent did the work, the prompts, the specification and the
session may be part of the record. Question 5 of
[the agent-written code document](agent-written-code.qmd) asks which.

### 3.11 Use

**Asks.** Was the answer used for the decision it was meant to inform, and
did the decision go the way the analysis said it should?

**Existing tools.** None. The
[PMX internship specification](../pmx-internship/specification.qmd)
checks use three months after an internship, for one project.

**Gap.** No practice of following an analysis to its decision. Without it,
nothing tells whether the validation upstream was at the right depth.

## 4. The Validation Plan

A validation plan is written at the start of an activity, next to its
specification, and filled in as the checks are done. One plan per activity:
a model fit, a simulation, a literature review, a dose recommendation.

The header records:

- **Activity** and the **decision** it informs.
- **Consequence of a wrong answer**, and how likely one is, as in the
  Validation Checklist's risk assessment.
- **Author**: the person or agent doing the work, and who directs the agent
  if there is one.

Then one row per kind from Section 3:

| # | Kind | Applies? | Tool | Depth | Checked by | Done |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Question | | | | | |
| 2 | Causal assumptions | | | | | |
| 3 | Sources | | | | | |
| ... | | | | | | |
| 11 | Use | | | | | |

: Validation plan, one row per kind {tbl-colwidths="[4,16,10,22,20,18,10]"}

**Depth** takes one of the Validation Checklist's levels: spot check,
review, rerun step by step, or independent reproduction. Every row is kept,
and a kind that does not apply says so with a reason, so that two plans can
be compared and an empty row is not read as a check that passed.

## 5. Gaps, Ranked

Ranked by how often the gap is likely to let a wrong answer through, which
is a judgment until Section 7 step 2 gives evidence.

1. **Data assembly checklist** (3.4). Data errors pass every later check.
2. **Model evaluation checklist** (3.6). Shared with the skills project.
3. **A causal diagram as a standing step** (3.2). The checklist exists;
   the gap is that no plan asks for it, so confounding is considered only
   when someone thinks of it.
4. **A benchmarking procedure** (3.7): which simple model, which held-out
   data, what difference counts.
5. **Checking claims against sources** (3.3), as a tool someone outside this
   repository can use, including on an agent's summaries.
6. **Code written by an agent** (3.5), already under way in
   [its own document](agent-written-code.qmd).
7. **The question after the work, and its use** (3.1, 3.11).
8. **Written reports** (3.9).

## 6. Open Questions

1. **Is "validation" the right word for all eleven kinds?** Regulatory and
   engineering usage separates verification (was it built right: kinds 4, 5
   and 10) from validation (is it the right thing: kinds 1, 2, 6 and 11). The
   taxonomy may read better in those terms.
2. **Does depth scale with the author?** For people it does: a senior
   associate's model gets a lighter review than an intern's. For an agent
   there is no track record per kind of task yet. The validation plans
   themselves, once kept, would build one.
3. **Can an agent do some of the checking?** A second agent reviewing the
   first may share its blind spots. Question 1 of
   [the agent-written code document](agent-written-code.qmd) asks the same
   for code; the question is wider here.
4. **Are eleven kinds the right number?** Missing candidates include safety and
   regulatory consistency (does the analysis agree with the label and with
   earlier submissions), and the author's understanding, which the
   internship's final presentation checks for a person.
5. **What prior art covers this?** The ASME V&V 40 standard sets the depth
   of credibility evidence for a computational model by its risk, the same
   move as the Validation Checklist's planning section, and the ICH M15
   guideline on model-informed drug development is reported to use a
   similar framework for PMX models. Neither has been read here.
6. **Does every model need a causal diagram?** A diagram for a
   population PK model, where the question is not causal, may be wasted
   time; a diagram for an exposure-response model usually is not. The
   lighter rule is that every plan considers one and says why when it
   skips it. Step 2 will show which rule holds up.

## 7. Steps

1. Read ASME V&V 40 and ICH M15 against Section 3 and start a
   `references.qmd`, shaped as the
   [TCE-IPDE references](../tce-ipde/references.qmd).
2. Fill in a validation plan for one past activity, the
   [Model Based TDP worked comparison](../pmx-model-based-tdp/index.qmd),
   and one for the next internship project. Record what each check caught.
3. Re-rank Section 5 from what step 2 found, and open a project for the gap
   at the top.
4. Once the template has been used twice, add it to the Validation section
   of the [Pharmacometrics Tools](../../pmx-tools.qmd) page.
